title: Capxul Protocol v4 scenario
description: A company's life as data (docs/planning/protocol-v4/spec/scenario-player.md). Read by the Foundry runner (test/scenario/Scenario_Test.t.sol) and the player (packages/scenarios/src/protocol-v4). An address argument or expectation is an address expression: an actor's name (a person's personal Safe, Companies House's Safe, the `anyone` account), `<actor>.signer` (the actor's own key), a contract name from `contracts`, or a 0x address.

at.description: An offset from `start` (`+<n>s`, `+<n>m` minutes, `+<n>h`, `+<n>d`, `+<n>w`) or an absolute UTC time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

units.description: Exact token units: digits, or digits e digits (600000e6).

oneOf.description: The role: `companies-house`, `anyone`, `company` (the company Safe, claimed for its email like a person's; its key installs money, then the Board acts for it), or any other word (founder, ops, employee) for a person.

email.description: A person's normalised email: their personal Safe is the one Companies House claims for `namespace` and this email.

amount.description: Exact units, or within a tolerance (the Capxul exit vectors match to within $1).

call.description: `<Contract>.<function>` with args by the interface's parameter names. Values: a uint is digits, digits e digits, a UTC time (its Unix seconds), an `ids` name or a hat (Board, Shareholders, Director, an officer's details); a bytes32 is 0x and 64 hex digits or text (its keccak256); an address is an address expression, a token, an `addresses` name, or `money.<field>` / `equity.<field>` of the recorded deployment; a struct may be `Installer.deployMoney` or `Installer.deployEquity` (what that call returned); any value may be `@name` (the `data` entry). Pseudo-calls: `Board.approveHash` (args {}: a Director's Safe approves the next `Board.execTransaction`'s company Safe transaction, ruling D1), `Board.execTransaction` ({ calls }: a Director's Safe executes it with v = 1 for itself and every Director who approved since the last batch), `Safe.batch` ({ calls }: the actor's own Safe runs them), `Governor.propose` ({ calls, description }), `Governor.castVote` ({ description, support }), `Governor.execute` ({ description }), `Payments.sendBatch` ({ exitSaleId, holdings }: the exit payouts `Exits.preview` gives). In a batch, `Installer.buildMoney` and `Installer.buildEquity` stand for the calls they return (buildEquity: the Safe's in a Board batch, the founder's in a Safe.batch); one plain call is sent as a call, anything else as a MultiSendCallOnly 1.4.1 delegatecall.

uint.description: Digits, digits e digits (600000e6), or a name (an `ids` entry or a hat).

start.description: The chain's clock is set here first.

namespace.description: The Companies House salt namespace of the people's personal Safes.

contracts.description: v4 contracts without constructor arguments that Companies House deploys first, each by CREATE2 with salt keccak256("capxul:v4:<Name>").

actors.description: Each actor by name. A person acts from their personal Safe (D1); companies-house acts as Companies House's Safe by delegatecall (D13); anyone acts from its own key. `anyone` needs no entry.

tokens.description: ERC-20s on the fork, by name (an address expression and a `<name>.approve` / `<name>.transfer` call target); `fund` sets balances at setup.

events.description: In time order; events at the same instant run in file order.

revert.description: The custom error the call must revert with: a bare name for an error without parameters, else its signature, e.g. `DerivedAddressMismatch(address,address)`.

checkpoints.description: In time order. A checkpoint runs after every event at or before its time.

Budgets.description: By budget name: amount, childrenAmount, ownSpent, ownCommitted, spent, committed (effective values), left, parent, hat.

balances.description: By address expression, then token name.

Agreements.description: By agreement name: collected, reserved, available, earned.

hats.description: By hat name, then address expression: whether it wears the hat.

shares.description: By address expression, then class name: the class token balance.

locked.description: By address expression, then class name: Vesting.lockedOf at the checkpoint.

classes.description: By class name: totalSupply, authorised, conversionPrice.

expect.description: Checked at the checkpoint; then every checkpoint re-checks B1, B2, B6, A1, A2 and P2 over the whole company, and E1 and E3 once equity is installed.

addresses.description: Third-party contracts by name (Hats, the Hats Signer Gate implementation, ...), usable as address expressions.

deploy.description: v4 contracts Companies House deploys after `contracts`, in order, each by CREATE2 with salt keccak256("capxul:v4:<name>"); `source` is the file under src/ (as deploy/manifest.json), `args` the constructor's arguments, all address expressions.

wire.description: Calls Companies House sends as plain calls right after the deploys (Budgets.setAgreements: only the deployer may).

ids.description: Names for ids (budgets, agreements, scheduled payments, classes, rounds, notes, grants, transfers, sales), each digits. Ids are what the contracts' counters give on a fresh deploy.

data.description: Values an argument names with `@name` (a struct shared by two events, an exit's holdings).
